articles.title: WWE Chief Triple H confirms Roman Reigns vs LA Knight World Heavyweight Championship for Money in the Bank
articles.summary: WWE News: WWE Chief Content Officer Triple H has reportedly confirmed that Roman Reigns is going to lock horns with LA Knight for the World Heavyweight Champion.
articles.body: WWE Chief Content Officer Triple H has reportedly confirmed that Roman Reigns is going to lock horns with LA Knight for the World Heavyweight Championship at Money in the Bank. Reigns will defend the World Heavyweight Championship against LA Knight at Money in the Bank 2026.The announcement comes after Knight attacked Reigns following his successful title defense against Penta on Monday Night RAW in Mexico City. The upcoming match will also allow LA Knight to challenge Reigns for a world championship after their previous encounters ended in disappointment for The Megastar.Roman Reigns is confirmed to be locking horns with LA Knight at Money in the Bank 2026 eventWWE Chief Content Officer Triple H has reportedly confirmed a new challenger for Roman Reigns in the upcoming World Heavyweight Championship at the Money in the Bank event, and the OTC will be locking horns with his long-time rival L.A. Knight.The major announcement comes after Knight attacked Reigns following his successful title defense against Penta on Monday Night Raw in Mexico City. Reigns entered Raw looking to retain his World Heavyweight Championship against Penta in the show.However, he gave his best despite facing a hostile crowd and defeated the challenger. The OGC managed to walk away with the title around his waist. However, Reigns's celebration did not last long.L.A. Knight appeared after the match and attacked the champion immediately after making his intentions clear. The confrontation prompted Raw General Manager Adam Pearce to announce that Reigns would put his championship on the line against Knight at Money in the Bank.Triple H has subsequently made the match official by sharing the bout's graphic for the upcoming premium live. The match will give Knight another opportunity to challenge Reigns for a world championship after the previous encounter ended in disappointment. In this match, L.A. Knight will finally get his one-on-one opportunity, because the rivalry dates back to 2023 when the two competed for the undisputed WWE Universal Championship at the Crown Jewel.However, Reigns managed to win that encounter with assistance from Bloodline. The two stars again crossed paths at the 2024 Royal Rumble, where Reigns defended his championship in a fatal four-way match against Knight, Randy Orton, and AJ Styles.Knight has always complained that he has never received a fair one-on-one opportunity to fight against Reigns. However, his latest confrontation appears to be finally earned in that chance.Also, Knight has made it clear that he wants a fair fight, while Reigns will be determined to continue his reign as the World Heavyweight Champion. With the Money in the Bank now officially set for October 10 in New Orleans, the WWE has gained another major storyline as Reigns will enter the event as champion, but L.A. Knight will have the opportunity to defy his long-running frustration and clinch the title from his rival in a career-defining victory.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fernando Alonso se pasea con un deslumbrante Bugatti Veyron pulido a espejo
articles.standfirst: El asturiano ha sido visto con un Bugatti Veyron del que podría haber solo cinco ejemplares en el mundo y cuyo precio podría situarse en unos dos millones de euros.
articles.summary: El asturiano ha sido visto con un Bugatti Veyron del que podría haber solo cinco ejemplares en el mundo y cuyo precio podría situarse en unos dos millones de euros.
articles.body: Fernando Alonso tiene un idilio con los coches más exclusivos del planeta. Y aunque por contrato se permite rodar con modelos de Aston Martin (el Valkyrie es su máxima expresión y el asturiano tiene un ejemplar de su propiedad), no pasa mucho tiempo sin que le veamos a los mandos de coches que ya no se fabrican y cuya cotización resulta estratosférica. Ahora bien, si son de su propiedad o en realidad pertenecen a alguien de su confianza que los pone en sus manos, es algo que en pocas ocasiones podemos conocer. El último ejemplar con el que se le ha visto, cómo no por las calles de Mónaco, es un Bugatti Veyron 16.4 con los paneles de la carrocería de aluminio pulido. Todo parece indicar que se trata de la versión Pur Sang. El Pur Sang mantiene el motor de 8,0 litros con cuatro turbos que desarrolla 1.001 CV y 1.250 Nm de par, lo que le capacita para rodar a 407 km/h y pasar de 0 a 100 en 2,5 segundos. Pero, a diferencia del Veyron 'normal', prescinde de la pintura y deja al descubierto el aluminio de su carrocería, esta vez pulida a espejo. Puede parecer un detalle menor, pero se trata de una excentricidad de la que solo se fabricaron cinco ejemplares en 2007, todos los cuales se vendieron en 24 horas a un precio aproximado de 1,4 millones de euros sin contar impuestos. El año pasado RM Sotheby's subastó uno de los ejemplares y el precio rozó los dos millones de euros. Sin embargo, hay un detalle que hace sospechar: los Pur Sang de carrocería pulida salieron de fábrica con un capó de fibra de carbono, mientras que en el Veyron que conduce Alonso el capó es también de aluminio pulido. ¿Es un Pur Sang auténtico y algún anterior propietario le cambió el capó? ¿Es un Veyron 16.4 convencional y en su momento fue sometido a un tratamiento de pulido similar al de los Pur Sang? Sería muy difícil saberlo, aunque en ambos casos la cotización del coche es desorbitada.

articles.title: Football on a curved table, wrestling without groundwork: Five little-known sports India will compete in at Asian Games 2026
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: The Asian Games have always been more than a showcase of the sports that dominate television screens.From cricket and hockey to athletics, shooting, b.
articles.body: The Asian Games have always been more than a showcase of the sports that dominate television screens.From cricket and hockey to athletics, shooting, badminton and wrestling, some disciplines have a deep following in India. But Aichi-Nagoya 2026 will also put the spotlight on sports that remain largely unfamiliar to the country's mainstream sporting audience.The 20th edition of the Asian Games will be held in Japan from September 19 to October 4, with around 11,000 athletes from 45 countries and regions competing across 43 sports. India will be represented by 503 athletes across a wide range of disciplines.Some of those sports are familiar internationally but still developing a following in India. Mixed martial arts, surfing, esports and padel, for instance, are expanding rapidly and have attracted growing global attention.Then there are sports such as Teqball, Kurash, Soft Tennis, Sepak Takraw and Sport Climbing.They may not yet command the same audience as cricket, badminton or hockey in India, but they will be part of the country's Asian Games campaign in Japan.So, what exactly are these sports?Teqball: When football meets table tennisIf football and table tennis were combined into one sport, the result might look something like Teqball.Played on a specially designed curved table, Teqball requires players to control and return a football using body parts other than the hands and arms. The sport combines football technique with the precision and rhythm associated with table tennis. Players can compete in singles or doubles, with a maximum of three touches before the ball has to be returned.The sport was developed in Hungary and has grown rapidly over the past decade.And Aichi-Nagoya will mark an important milestone: Teqball is making its Asian Games debut as a medal sport. The Olympic Council of Asia added it to the 2026 programme in March.India will have three representatives: Mohamed Anas Imran Beg, Declan Marshall Gonsalves and Quimcy Dsouza. They will compete in men's doubles, mixed doubles and women's singles.A football becomes the object of a game that looks part tennis rally, part freestyle football and part table-tennis exchange.Kurash: The wrestling sport where the fight stays on its feetKurash may look familiar to anyone who has watched judo or wrestling, but its rules create a distinctly different contest.An ancient jacket-wrestling tradition from Central Asia, particularly associated with Uzbekistan, Kurash is built around throws rather than ground fighting.The defining feature is simple: the contest remains standing.Competitors wear jackets and belts and attempt to throw their opponent onto the back. Groundwork is not permitted, while techniques such as striking, kicking, choking and joint locks are prohibited.That makes Kurash a fast and explosive sport. There is little of the prolonged ground grappling that audiences might associate with some other combat disciplines. The emphasis is on grip, balance, timing, strength and the ability to execute a clean throw.Kurash has been part of the Asian Games programme in recent editions, and India already has a small but significant history in the sport.India won two Kurash medals at the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta-Palembang, both in the women's 52kg category. Pincky Balhara won silver and Malaprabha Jadhav took bronze.India's Aichi-Nagoya squad includes Vipin Kumar in men's -66kg, Vishal and Yash Kumar in men's +90kg, Bharti and Sangita Balhara in women's -57kg, and Pincky Chauhan in women's -78kg.For Indian viewers accustomed to wrestling, judo and kabaddi, Kurash is perhaps one of the easier sports to understand once the central rule is known: get the opponent off balance, throw them cleanly and stay on your feet.Soft Tennis: It looks like tennis, but the ball changes everythingAt first glance, Soft Tennis can be mistaken for ordinary tennis.The court and net are broadly familiar. The players use rackets. The objective is still to hit the ball into the opponent's court.But the equipment and playing characteristics are different.Soft Tennis uses a lightweight, air-filled rubber ball rather than the heavier felt-covered ball used in conventional tennis. According to the International Soft Tennis Federation, the ball weighs between 30 and 31 grams. That softer, lighter ball changes the rhythm of the game.Soft Tennis originated in Japan in the late 19th century and subsequently spread across Asia. It has been part of the Asian Games programme since 1994.The scoring system is also different from conventional tennis. Rather than the familiar 15-30-40 sequence, Soft Tennis uses numerical scoring, making the scoring easier to follow for newcomers.India has competed in Soft Tennis at previous Asian Games but is yet to win a medal. Aichi-Nagoya will therefore provide another opportunity to break that drought.India's six-member squad comprises Yogesh Choudhary, Om Yadav, Jay Meena, Aniket Chirag Patel, Aryan Thakur and Aadhya Tiwari. They will compete across the men's team event, men's singles and mixed doubles, with Aadhya also entered in women's singles.Sepak Takraw: Football skills on a volleyball courtFew Asian sports can produce moments as spectacular as Sepak Takraw.The sport combines elements of volleyball with the kicking, heading and acrobatic skills associated with football.Two teams compete across a net, with three players forming a regu. The court is similar in dimensions to a badminton court, while the players are not allowed to use their hands or arms.Feet, knees, chest and head become the main tools.Each side has a maximum of three touches to control the ball and send it back over the net. The attacking player can then launch into spectacular aerial movements — including scissor kicks and bicycle-kick-style strikes — to send the ball beyond the defence.The result is one of the most visually striking sports on the Asian Games programme.Sepak Takraw has been part of the Asian Games since 1990, but it remains relatively unfamiliar to large sections of the Indian sporting audience.India, however, has been gradually building a record in the discipline.The country has won two Asian Games bronze medals so far: a men's Team Regu bronze at Jakarta-Palembang 2018 and a women's Regu bronze at Hangzhou 2022.India will field both men's and women's teams in Aichi-Nagoya, with the men's squad competing in Team Regu and Quadrant events.The men's contingent includes Arun, Jasvir, Ashish Chundawat, Shyam Singh, Lokhon Singh Elangbam, Bobby Kumar, Ashok Singh Mayengbam, Ram Kumar Sharma, O Amarjit Singha, Malemnganba Singh Sorokhaibam, Henary Singh Wahengbam and Akash Yumnam.The women's contingent includes players such as Leirentonbi Devi Elangbam, Prity Langoljam, Menenu Tsukru, Maipak Devi Ayekpam, Priya Devi Elangbam, Shilpa Elangbam, Chaoba Devi Oinam, Seyiekhrieno Tepa and Malemnganbi Yumnam.For India, Sepak Takraw is no longer an entirely new experiment. The medals in the last two editions have already provided a foundation.Sport Climbing: Speed, strength and a race against gravitySport Climbing may be the most visually recognisable of the five to younger audiences, thanks in part to its growing international profile.At the Asian Games, climbers compete on artificial walls, using strength, balance, flexibility, technique and problem-solving ability to navigate routes covered with coloured holds.There are three disciplines: Speed, Boulder and Lead.Speed is exactly what it sounds like. Climbers race side-by-side up an identical 15-metre wall, with the fastest time deciding the winner.Boulder is different. Climbers tackle shorter, difficult routes without ropes, relying on technique and problem-solving to complete the designated problems.Lead takes the contest higher. Climbers attempt to ascend a wall more than 12 metres high, with the result determined by how high they manage to climb within the allotted time.The three disciplines test different qualities. Speed is about explosive acceleration and precision. Boulder is about solving a physical puzzle. Lead combines endurance, strength and route-reading.Sport Climbing made its Asian Games debut at Jakarta-Palembang 2018. India has competed in the sport at the last two editions but is yet to win an Asian Games medal.At Aichi-Nagoya, India's representatives include Deepu Mallesh in men's speed and Joga Purty in women's speed.More than just unfamiliar namesThe five sports represent different sides of the Asian Games.Teqball is a young hybrid sport trying to establish itself on the global stage. Kurash carries centuries of Central Asian tradition into a modern competitive format. Soft Tennis demonstrates how a familiar sport can develop a distinct identity through different equipment and rules. Sepak Takraw showcases Southeast Asia's spectacular athletic culture. Sport Climbing brings strength, speed and problem-solving together on a vertical stage.They also underline why the Asian Games remain different from the Olympics.The continental Games have traditionally provided space for sports rooted in particular regions as well as newer disciplines seeking wider international recognition. Aichi-Nagoya's programme includes 43 sports, with Teqball among the new additions and established Asian disciplines such as Kurash, Sepak Takraw and Soft Tennis continuing to feature.For Indian fans, that means the next few weeks will offer more than the familiar medal races.There will be moments when a curved table, a jacket throw, a soft rubber ball, an airborne kick or a climber racing up a wall suddenly becomes the centre of attention.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Live Updates: Gonsalves-Beg pair starts India’s Asian Games campaign with teqball
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 Live Updates: India will begin its Asian Games 2026 campaign today, two days before the official opening ceremony in Aichi-Nagoya, J
articles.body: Asian Games 2026 Live: Despite Neeraj Chopra’s absence, Indian athletics could turn in a fine show Javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra, who led India’s 1-2 finish in the men’s event at the last Asian Games in Hangzhou, is out with an injury. Two-time defending champion in men’s shot put Tajinderpal Singh is not in his best form and women’s javelin throw gold medallist Annu Rani failed to make the cut. Will it then be a tough outing for India’s athletes? The answer could surprise many because the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) has nurtured a new breed of talented athletes capable of repeating or even improving the performance from the last edition of the Games held in China..Asian Games 2026 Live: Indian athletes land in Japan to a forgettable welcome Japan’s reputation for organisational efficiency lay in tatters as the rowing and shooting contingent faced unexpected ordeals upon arrival. A majority of the rowing squad were left stranded without accommodation, some of their names actually missing from the accreditation system. “Only three of the 22 men’s athletes have accommodation against their names. And the names of three of the five women rowers (Poonam, Aleena Anto and Anshika Bharati) are not registered with the hosts even though they all have valid accreditation,” said a Rowing Federation of India (RFI) official..Asian Games 2026 Live: India schedule today (IST) Teqball Men’s doubles Group B: Declan Marshall Gonsalves/Mohamed Anas Imran Beg vs Truong Giang Ba/Anh Khoa Le (Vietnam) - 12:30 PM Men’s doubles Group B: Declan Marshall Gonsalves/Mohamed Anas Imran Beg vs Junsuk Lee/Taebeen Lee (Republic of Korea) - 1:00 PM Men’s doubles quarter-finals: Gonsalves/Beg (subject to qualification) - 3:30 PM onwards Men’s doubles repechage: Gonsalves/Beg (subject to qualification) - 4:00 PM onwards.Asian Games 2026 Live: Three Indians in teqball’s five medal events Teqball will feature five medal events at Aichi-Nagoya 2026 — men’s singles, women’s singles, men’s doubles, women’s doubles and mixed doubles — with competition running from September 17 to 20. Each event begins with a round-robin group stage before moving into the knockout rounds, which also include a repechage pathway. India have three athletes competing across these events. Besides partnering Gonsalves in the men’s doubles, Anas Imran Beg will team up with Quimcy Dsouza in the mixed doubles, while Dsouza will also compete in the women’s singles. Although the Asian Games officially run from September 19 to October 4, several sports, including teqball, begin competition before the opening ceremony, giving India an early opportunity to make an impact at the Aichi-Nagoya Games..Asian Games 2026 Live: Five little-known sports India will compete in The Asian Games have always been more than a showcase of the sports that dominate television screens. From cricket and hockey to athletics, shooting, badminton and wrestling, some disciplines have a deep following in India. But Aichi-Nagoya 2026 will also put the spotlight on sports that remain largely unfamiliar to the country's mainstream sporting audience. The 20th edition of the Asian Games will be held in Japan from September 19 to October 4, with around 11,000 athletes from 45 countries and regions competing across 43 sports. India will be represented by 503 athletes across a wide range of disciplines. Some of those sports are familiar internationally but still developing a following in India. Mixed martial arts, surfing, esports and padel, for instance, are expanding rapidly and have attracted growing global attention. Then there are sports such as Teqball, Kurash, Soft Tennis, Sepak Takraw and Sport Climbing. They may not yet command the same audience as cricket, badminton or hockey in India, but they will be part of the country's Asian Games campaign in Japan..Asian Games 2026 Live: World Championships medallists eye knockout stage Gonsalves and Beg will enter the men’s doubles competition with international experience behind them, having already made history as India’s first World Championships medallists in teqball. The pair won a bronze medal in men’s doubles at the 2024 World Championships in Vietnam and will now look to carry that momentum into the sport’s Asian Games debut. Drawn in Group B, the Indians are scheduled to face Vietnam’s Truong Giang Ba and Anh Khoa Le in their opening match at 12:30 PM IST at the Nagoya City Higashi Sports Center. They will then take on the Republic of Korea’s Junsuk Lee and Taebeen Lee at 1:00 PM IST. The top contenders will then move into the knockout stage, with the competition also offering a repechage route..Asian Games 2026 Live: Teqball gives India an early start India’s Asian Games 2026 campaign will get underway with teqball, two days before the official opening ceremony in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. The Indian men’s doubles pair of Declan Marshall Gonsalves and Mohamed Anas Imran Beg will be the country’s first athletes in action at the continental Games today. Invented in Hungary, teqball combines elements of football and table tennis, with players using a curved table to exchange the ball without letting it touch the ground. The sport can broadly be described as a blend of freestyle football and sepak takraw, played on a curved, table tennis-style surface. Teqball will make its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya 2026, adding an unfamiliar but increasingly popular discipline to the competition..Asian Games 2026 Live: A floating athletes' village — and an unprecedented security operation The logistics of accommodating such a huge gathering have produced one of the most unusual features of Aichi-Nagoya 2026: there is no conventional dedicated athletes' village. Instead, as many as 5,000 athletes and officials are expected to stay aboard the Italian cruise liner Costa Serena, while others will be accommodated in hotels and temporary wooden containers. Organisers had initially planned for around 15,000 athletes and officials, but the registered number reportedly rose to about 17,000 around August. The accommodation crunch has been compounded by late arrivals, new sports such as teqball and padel, and the varying sizes of delegations. China is sending around 815 representatives, while Hong Kong, despite having a population of only about 7.5 million, is sending roughly 580. Security will be another huge undertaking, with Japanese media reporting that around 10,000 police and security personnel will be deployed around Saturday's opening ceremony in Nagoya, which will be attended by Emperor Naruhito and Empress Masako..Asian Games 2026 Live: Neeraj Chopra's absence changes the javelin equation The men's javelin throw will have an intriguing South Asian dimension, particularly after Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage produced a major breakthrough on the international stage. Pathirage recently won the javelin competition at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest, putting him in a strong position heading into the Asian Games. His emergence has added another name to a discipline that has been dominated by some of the continent's biggest athletics stars. Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem, the defending Olympic champion, is also expected to compete, although he finished fifth in Budapest. India's Neeraj Chopra, the Tokyo 2020 Olympic champion, will not be part of the Aichi-Nagoya field after missing the Games with an ankle injury. His absence removes one of the biggest names from the event, while Pathirage's recent form and Nadeem's pedigree set up an interesting contest for continental supremacy..Asian Games 2026 Live: Alex Eala puts Asian Games gold ahead of a major WTA event For some athletes, the attraction of the Asian Games goes beyond rankings and individual tournament schedules. Philippine tennis star Alex Eala is an example. The world No. 18 is expected to compete in Aichi-Nagoya after choosing to skip the WTA 1000 China Open, a mandatory tournament on the women's tennis calendar. Eala has spoken enthusiastically about representing the Philippines and described competing alongside her national team as a particularly enjoyable experience. Her attachment to multi-sport events was also evident when she reflected on last year's Southeast Asian Games, saying certain memories from that competition had stayed with her. The Asian Games are held only once every four years, making them a rare opportunity to compete for a continental title as part of a national delegation. Eala already has two bronze medals from Hangzhou and will now chase a step higher on the podium, even though skipping a mandatory WTA event could carry ranking and financial consequences..Asian Games 2026 Live: Badminton brings Olympic champions into the spotlight Badminton is one of the sports that can give the Asian Games an atmosphere closer to a major global championship, particularly because some of Asia's biggest stars compete for continental honours. South Korea's An Se-young is one of the leading names in the field. The women's singles Olympic champion from Paris is also the world's top-ranked player and arrives with an imposing recent record. She won the women's singles gold medal at the Hangzhou Asian Games three years ago and also contributed to South Korea's team gold. Her form remains strong after another China Masters title, her third in succession, and a world title earlier this year. Yet An has suggested that the Asian Games carry a different kind of significance. She told South Korean news agency Yonhap that the event could feel similar to other international tournaments, but reaching the top of the podium would mean hearing her country's national anthem — a distinction that gives the Games an added emotional dimension..Asian Games 2026 Live: China dominates — and swimming could produce more fireworks If there is one sporting power that has traditionally defined the Asian Games, it is China. At the Hangzhou Games, China won a staggering 201 gold medals, compared with 52 for Japan and 42 for South Korea, underlining the scale of its dominance. That pattern is expected to continue in Aichi-Nagoya, with swimming among the sports likely to attract major attention during the opening days. China is expected to field several Olympic champions, including Pan Zhanle, Wang Shun, Qin Haiyang and Xu Jiayu. Pan holds the world record in the men's 100m freestyle, while Qin has the global mark in the 200m breaststroke. There is also considerable curiosity around China's teenage swimming sensation Yu Zidi. At just 12, she finished fourth in three events at the 2025 World Championships in Singapore. Now 13, she will be among the young athletes attracting attention as the Asian Games swimming programme gets underway..Asian Games 2026 Live: From New Delhi 1951 to Aichi-Nagoya 2026 The Asian Games have come a long way since the inaugural edition was held in New Delhi in 1951. Aichi-Nagoya 2026 will mark the 20th edition of the continental multi-sport event, which has grown dramatically in both participation and sporting scope over the decades. The previous edition was held in Hangzhou, China, in 2023 after being postponed by a year because of the Covid-19 pandemic. Around 12,000 athletes took part in those Games, underlining how the Asian Games have developed into one of the world's biggest multi-sport events. The 2026 edition will again bring together athletes from across the continent, with 45 countries and regions represented. While the Olympics remain the bigger global sporting spectacle in terms of reach and profile, the Asian Games provide a much broader competitive platform for athletes from nations that rarely feature prominently at the Olympics..Asian Games 2026 Live: Bigger than the Summer Olympics in numbers The sheer scale of the Asian Games can be difficult to grasp until it is put alongside the Olympics. The 2024 Paris Summer Olympics featured around 10,700 athletes, while the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games are set to welcome more than 11,000 athletes when the event opens in Japan on Saturday. That figure could rise further, with organisers acknowledging a late surge in the number of athletes and officials travelling to the Games. The increase has already created pressure on accommodation and logistics. The Asian Games, therefore, are not simply a continental version of the Olympics in terms of sporting prestige; in terms of numbers, venues, accommodation, transport and daily operations, they represent an enormous undertaking. With delegations arriving from across Asia, the scale becomes even more apparent..Asian Games 2026 Live: India's campaign begins today Hello and welcome to the live coverage of the Asian Games 2026 from Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. India’s campaign gets underway two days before the official opening ceremony, with teqball marking the country’s first action at the continental Games today. Indian men’s doubles pair Declan Marshall Gonsalves and Mohamed Anas Imran Beg will be the first Indian athletes to take the field, as they begin their campaign in the historic Asian Games debut of teqball.

articles.title: NCAA admits replay errors but reiterates it cannot change result of Western Michigan-Michigan game
articles.summary: Western Michigan and its conference have insisted Michigan should not have been given an extra second in its dramatic win over the Broncos two weeks ago.
articles.body: Western Michigan and its conference have insisted Michigan should not have been given an extra second in its dramatic win over the Broncos two weeks ago. The NCAA agrees, but said it can’t do anything about it. The NCAA Football Bowl Subdivision Oversight Committee announced Wednesday that proper replay protocols weren’t followed in Michigan’s Hail Mary win, altering the outcome of the game. The committee also reiterated what the NCAA said last week: It doesn’t have the authority to overturn the result. “The committee consulted with national officiating leadership regarding the instant replay protocols,” the committee said in a statement. “Based on that information, the committee agreed that the instant replay protocols were not followed in the contest’s second-to-last play,” the statement continued. “Had the protocols been followed, the outcome of the game would have been different.” Michigan, now ranked No. 19, won the September 5 game 13-12 on a Hail Mary pass after the replay official had put 1 second back on the clock when Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood’s first try was incomplete. The Mid-American Conference initially accepted the Big Ten’s explanation of what happened at the end of the game, but joined Western Michigan in asking for the result to be overturned. A few hours later, the NCAA said the result would stand, noting its playing rules do not have a protocol for overturning the outcome of a game and the oversight committee does not have the authority to do so, which it confirmed again on Wednesday. “The playing rules governing the result of a contest are clear: once the referee declares a contest to be final, no appeal of the outcome is permitted, according to (rules),” the committee said.

articles.title: Chess Olympiad: How India's Arjun Erigaisi suffered biggest Round 1 upset against lower-rated opponent
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: Arjun Erigaisi (rated 2759) is India's second-ranked chess player at the moment. On Wednesday, with R Praggnanandhaa, India's current No. 1.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Arjun Erigaisi (rated 2759) is India's second-ranked chess player at the moment. On Wednesday, with R Praggnanandhaa, India's current No. 1, rested, the 23-year-old Telangana grandmaster took Board 1 for India at the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.India's opposition was Thailand, whose top board was occupied by 2363-rated International Master Prin Laohawirapap, the Thai No. 1. With a rating gap of almost 400 Elo points, and Arjun holding the white pieces, the result looked a formality.Instead, it became one of the biggest Round 1 upsets in Olympiad history. Chess.com even made the Thai IM's win over Arjun its Game of the Day, with only Iraqi CM Ali Ehsan Aryan's draw against Levon Aronian coming close as an upset against a 2700-rated grandmaster.How Arjun lost the plot"The Indian grandmaster playing white started the game with the Colle system, which is not necessarily one of the sharpest systems. He got a slight advantage from the position," veteran Grandmaster Pravin Thipsay told TimesofIndia.com while analysing the game.The first real opening came on move 18."The Thai player made a serious error of judgement by playing Rook e8. Instead of the 18th move, black taking on f5, e into f5, would have led to equality. But after Rook e8, Arjun was in a very powerful position," he assessed.At that stage, Thipsay noted, the win looked routine as Arjun was gaining considerable time advantage on the clock as well. However, it was move 28 that changed things."Instead of launching a pawn roller with h4 on the 28th move, Arjun chose to trade the black knight which had come to his territory, and Bxd3 turned out to be a mistake which led to an equal position," the grandmaster told this website.Thailand's Prin then returned the favour."On the 31st move, now it was the Thailand player who made a serious mistake," Thipsay said. "He could have probably equalised. There is no direct kingside attack coming. The move chosen by the Thailand player was really very dangerous. It weakened his kingside, and Arjun was in a completely winning position thereafter."What followed was a masterclass in resourcefulness from the lower-rated player."The Thai player really played resourcefully and was successful in complicating the game. The Thai player offered a rook, an exchange as we call it, rook for knight, on move 46-47," he explained."By taking the rook, knight into e4 on move 47, Arjun could have won the game. Though his king was very exposed, and it might have led to a perpetual check or something else. But yes, white had a decisive advantage with accurate play had he taken the rook with knight into e4. Instead, he played knight f3, not taking the rook, which led to a drawish position."Even then, the half point was there. It was ambition that cost him."In the drawish position, again at move 50, Arjun played the ambitious move Qg7, trying to checkmate the opponent, which allowed a very basic checkmate to black. By playing the 50th move Qf4, Arjun could have defended himself and the game would have ended in a draw. But after the move played, Qg7, he got checkmated very fast," Thipsay added."Quite an unexpected result considering the difference of around 400 rating points, a great setback for Arjun."India earn convincing wins in both categoriesArjun Erigaisi's defeat, however, did not affect India's overall team score. Gukesh, Nihal Sarin, and Vidit Gujrathi all defeated their opponents, helping India seal a 3–1 team victory.The Indian women's team, with Divya Deshmukh rested, produced an even more dominant performance, defeating the Dominican Republic 4–0.India was among nine of the top 10 seeds to record clean sweeps on the opening day of the Women's Olympiad. Germany was the only team among the top 10 seeds to drop a game, narrowly defeating Malta 3–1.India, defending champions in both sections, play Indonesia in the Open on Thursday, while the women's team takes on Finland.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Indian athletes land in Japan to a forgettable welcome
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Japan’s reputation for organisational efficiency lay in tatters as the rowing and shooting contingent faced unexpected ordeals upon arrival. A majorit.
articles.body: Japan’s reputation for organisational efficiency lay in tatters as the rowing and shooting contingent faced unexpected ordeals upon arrival. A majority of the rowing squad were left stranded without accommodation, some of their names actually missing from the accreditation system.“Only three of the 22 men’s athletes have accommodation against their names. And the names of three of the five women rowers (Poonam, Aleena Anto and Anshika Bharati) are not registered with the hosts even though they all have valid accreditation,” said a Rowing Federation of India (RFI) official.The rowers’ nightmare had actually begun even before they boarded their flight. One of the groups that left Mumbai on Tuesday night was told by Cathay Pacific that they would not be allowed to check in their oars. Later, the oars were flown to Delhi. They will arrive in Nagoya on Thursday morning, just in time for the first official practice session.Adding to the agony was the Sports Authority of India’s belated intimation that women’s coach Ratheesh Kumar and team manager Ramakrishnan Ramachandran would have to manage their accommodation on their own.Meanwhile, the shooters had to wait for almost three hours for their transport after reaching the Nagoya airport at 9 pm on Tuesday. “We didn’t get the bus and there was no food. Everything was closed at the airport. The welcome centre had no information, so we had to wait and reach the hotel around 4 am,” a team member told TOI.Samaresh gets wrong accreditationIndia’s pistol shooting head coach Samaresh Jung was in for a rude shock when he came to know his accreditation didn’t allow him to enter the players arena and the field of play during the matches. “It was a shock when we saw Samaresh’s accreditation. When we enquired, we were told that this was done according to the list the organisers had received from the Indian Olympic Association,” a source said.“We contacted our office at the National Rifle Association of India, and the issue was taken up. We are told that Samaresh will be getting the new accreditation tomorrow,” the source said. Samaresh’s absence would dent India’s medal chances as most of the 10m air pistol shooters like Suruchi Phogat, Akash Bhardwaj have been training under him.Citing shortage of govt funds, riders left to foot horse feed billIndian equestrian riders who are preparing for the Asian Games have been left scrambling to arrange hay, bedding and fodder for their horse combinations, with the Indian Olympic Association (IOA)-appointed ad-hoc committee running the sport citing a “shortage of govt funds”, reports Sabi Hussain.A mail accessed by TOI, signed by Lt Col Sandeep Dewan, member (administration), ad-hoc panel and team leader of the equestrian contingent, states that funds released to the national federation have been largely insufficient even to clear the bill of transporter Peden Bloodstock. The federation, the mail adds, has covered the shortfall from its own funds.“We regret to inform you that the govt has so far not released any funds for payment of feed and other expenses related to the maintenance of the horses whilst in Japan,” Dewan wrote.The riders have been asked to purchase feed and other stable requirements directly and claim reimbursement later.The financial strain extends beyond Japan. Riders said they had personally borne expenses for food, travel, accommodation and fees during the horses’ mandatory quarantine in Germany.Reimbursements for pre-quarantine tests, blood and swab tests, horse transportation, athlete accommodation and groom accommodation also remain pending. “Timely support on these essential matters is extremely important for us to focus completely on our performance in the Asian Games,” a rider told TOI on Wednesday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Despite Neeraj Chopra’s absence, Indian athletics could turn in a fine show
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra, who led India’s 1-2 finish in the men’s event at the last Asian Games in Hangzhou, is out with an injury. Two-time defe.
articles.body: Javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra, who led India’s 1-2 finish in the men’s event at the last Asian Games in Hangzhou, is out with an injury. Two-time defending champion in men’s shot put Tajinderpal Singh is not in his best form and women’s javelin throw gold medallist Annu Rani failed to make the cut. Will it then be a tough outing for India’s athletes?The answer could surprise many because the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) has nurtured a new breed of talented athletes capable of repeating or even improving the performance from the last edition of the Games held in China.Gulveer, the new starThe focus will be on Gulveer Singh, who has now risen in stature as is earning recognition among the finest long distance runners India has produced. The Services runner, who trains in the US, settled for the bronze medal in the last Games but this time he will start as a gold medal contender. Gulveer’s time of 27 minutes, 24.28s clocked in March, is the 12th fastest in the world this season.Usha’s record under threatIn the women’s section, athletics fans will be gunning for an Indian double in the long jump and the 400m hurdles. Ancy Sojan will be the flag bearer in the long jump. Her big leap of 6.88m at the National Inter-State athletics meet erased Anju Bobby George’s long-standing mark of 6.83m set in 1994. Shaili Singh is expected to give Ancy a strong challenge. So far, it has been Ancy all the way but Shaili is capable of producing an upset win.The oldest record in Indian athletics, PT Usha’s 55.42s in the women’s 400m hurdles, will again come under threat with last edition’s bronze winner Vithya Ramraj and Anu Raghavan, whose standing at the 2010 Games was upgraded from 4th to third, ready for a grand stand finish. Both clocked their season’s best in Bhubaneswar in June; Vithya won the race in 56.07s and Anu finished second in 56.54s.Sreeshankar, Kushare and TejaswinThe trio of Murali Sreeshankar (8.38m, Asian leader, men’s long jump), Sarvesh Anil Kushare (2.31m Asian lead, men’s high jump) and Tejaswin Shankar (8057 points, Asia second, decathlon) will all eye the top step on the podium.With impressive performances this season, the trio will look to add a title here to their collection. The return of Avinash Sable (defending champion in men’s 3000m steeplechase), after missing the Commonwealth Games, will be watched keenly.The other medal contenders include Sawan Barwal (men’s marathon), Praveen Chitravel (men’s triple jump), Rohit Yadav (men’s javelin throw), Toor (men’s shot put), Parul Chaudhary (women’s 5000m) and Jyothi Yarraji (women’s 100m hurdles), men’s 4x400m relay, women’s 4x400m relay and mixed 4x400m relay teams.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Women boxers will corner the glory at Asian Games: Vijender Singh
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: The gloves have barely cooled after India’s record-breaking 2026 Commonwealth Games campaign, but Vijender Singh knows the real examination.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The gloves have barely cooled after India’s record-breaking 2026 Commonwealth Games campaign, but Vijender Singh knows the real examination begins now.As India heads to AichiNagoya, the former Olympic and World Championships bronze medallist sounded a note of caution.“In comparison with the Commonwealth Games, the Asian Games will be tough for our boxers. They’re in good form, doing great but Asian Games will be different and far more difficult,” Vijender told TOI.His assessment comes at a particularly interesting moment. Indian boxing returned from Glasgow with seven gold medals and three silver — its best-ever haul at a Commonwealth Games. Among those who climbed to the top of the podium were Sachin Siwach, Sakshi Chaudhary, Preeti Pawar and Priya Ghanghas, three of whom Vijender identified as key medal hopes for Aichi-Nagoya.The challenge is that the Asian ring brings a different kind of pressure. China, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and Japan have traditionally provided some of the continent’s deepest boxing strength, with several of their fighters also operating at the Olympic level. Yet, Vijender expects India to return with a healthy medal haul, though he sees the women leading the charge.“I think our boxers can get three to four medals from the Asian Games. Let’s say, I’m expecting two-three from the girls and one or two medals can be clinched by the boys too.”His confidence in the women is understandable. Sakshi, Preeti and Priya arrive in Aichi-Nagoya after gold-medal performances in Glasgow.“Among the men, Sachin (Siwach) is a strong medal hope for India. Then there is (Narender) Berwal, who won bronze at the 2022 Asian Games. He also won the Arjuna award recently.“But my favourites are the girls. There is Sakshi (Chaudhary), Preeti (Pawar), who are strong contenders, and I also think that Priya Ghanghas is going to perform really well at the Asian Games. Coaches, trainers, who I’ve spoken to, have been raving about these three women boxers,” Vijender said.Siwach and Berwal, too, will go to Aichi-Nagoya with fresh evidence of their rising credentials. Siwach won the 60kg gold in Glasgow, while Berwal took silver in the 90kg plus category.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Deeply regrets': FIDE apologises over Chess Olympiad lodging crisis, assures teams of compensation
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: FIDE has stepped in to address an accommodation crisis that disrupted the opening day of the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, assuring aff.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: FIDE has stepped in to address an accommodation crisis that disrupted the opening day of the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, assuring affected federations that they will not be left to bear additional costs arising from the arrangements.In a statement, FIDE said it “notes with deep regret” that shortcomings in accommodation arrangements left some participating teams without proper lodging, forcing them to arrange rooms in the city at their own expense.While accommodation is the responsibility of the local Organising Committee (LOC), FIDE said it considered it its duty to assist the federations affected by the situation.The governing body has secured additional financial resources and confirmed that teams forced to arrange their own accommodation will be reimbursed for rooms of an appropriate standard for up to three days.FIDE also announced compensation for teams staying in official hotels that do not meet the standards approved for the Olympiad.“FIDE deeply regrets that these organizational problems occurred and apologizes to the affected federations and teams,” the statement said, adding that its priority was to ensure that no federation suffered financial losses because of the organisational shortcomings.The crisis also affected India's contingent, which arrived in Uzbekistan on Tuesday ahead of the opening round. Several members of the team were left waiting for hours after their reservations at the Silk Road by Minyoun hotel had not been properly communicated to the property by the LOC.Men's team captain Srinath Narayanan publicly raised the issue, while All India Chess Federation (AICF) president Nitin Narang held discussions with FIDE and the organising committee to resolve the situation. Head of Delegation Grandmaster Abhijit Kunte was also sent to assist the team on the ground.“We took up the matter very strongly with both the LOC and FIDE. In very simple terms, it was communicated that this was not acceptable and that this situation should never have happened in the first place.” Narang told TimesofIndia.com afterwards. "But I am relieved that the players have now been accommodated and are finally in their rooms."Vidit Gujrathi described the episode as a “very poor first impression” of the Samarkand Olympiad.ALSO READ: Chess Olympiad: How India's Arjun Erigaisi suffered biggest Round 1 upset against lower-rated opponentIndia arrive at the tournament as defending champions in both the Open and Women's sections after their historic double-gold triumph at the 2024 Budapest Olympiad. articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: MUMBAI: Amid growing calls for a leadership change in Indian women’s cricket, former India captain Anjum Chopra has backed Harmanpreet Kaur to continu.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Amid growing calls for a leadership change in Indian women’s cricket, former India captain Anjum Chopra has backed Harmanpreet Kaur to continue leading the side, insisting she remains the best person for the job despite recent scrutiny over her form.Harmanpreet scored 71 runs in five matches at the Women’s T20 Asia Cup in Dubai, where India lifted a record-extending eighth title. With the skipper now 37 and vice-captain Smriti Mandhana 30, suggestions of a transition in leadership have gathered momentum.Chopra, however, believes Harmanpreet remains India’s best captain. “People keep talking about changing the captain, but somebody has to lead every Indian team. As of now, Harmanpreet is the best captain to lead India,” Chopra told TOI.While acknowledging that Harmanpreet’s batting in Dubai fell below expectations, Chopra warned against judging the veteran solely on recent returns. “We always expect a special innings from her, something that reminds us of the 171 not out she scored against Australia in the 2017 World Cup. But that won’t happen every time,” she said.Chopra is confident the experienced batter will rediscover her rhythm as India build towards the inaugural Women’s Champions Trophy in 2027. “She knows fluency with the bat will be important going into major tournaments. The upcoming assignments, including the Asian Games and future bilateral series, will help her get there. She may be on the other side of 30, but India still need her services as captain and batter,” Chopra said.Fresh from an unbeaten Asia Cup campaign, India enter the Asian Games in Japan as defending champions and overwhelming favourites. Chopra believes adapting quickly to unfamiliar conditions will be their biggest challenge.“Understanding the pitches, environment and playing conditions will be crucial. On paper, India have a stronger side than the other Asian teams, but no tournament can be taken lightly. If they adapt well and play to their strengths, they should start as favourites,” she said.Chopra also praised Shafali Verma, who topped the scoring charts at the Asia Cup with 236 runs at a strike rate of 171.01 and three half-centuries.(Watch the Asian Games 2026 live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV.)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games: NADA panel’s interim order gives Abhishek Pal reprieve
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: BENGALURU: Long-distance runner Abhishek Pal’s hopes of competing at the Asian Games received a big boost after the Anti-Doping Disciplinary Panel of .
articles.body: BENGALURU: Long-distance runner Abhishek Pal’s hopes of competing at the Asian Games received a big boost after the Anti-Doping Disciplinary Panel of National Anti-Doping Agency clarified that there is no suspension that prevents the athlete from competing. Pal won the 10,000m gold and 5,000m silver at the inter-state meet in June but Athletics Federation of India (AFI) dropped him from the Asiad squad, citing adverse analytical findings in a National AntiDoping Agency (NADA) report.Hearing Pal’s appeal, the panel refused to quash the Notice of Charge but ordered a final hearing within four weeks. “No provisional suspension has been imposed on the athlete. The status quo as of today shall be maintained until the final disposal of this case,” the panel said in its interim order on Tuesday. The panel noted that “the athlete is not suspended and may continue to participate in competitions, subject to the final outcome of these proceedings.”In its observations and findings, the panel stated that “the athlete’s follow-up doping control tests conducted on June 7, June 21 and June 24 have all returned negative . The athlete’s previous test on May 6 was also negative. The athlete has been tested about 20 times and all results are negative. These are relevant circumstances to be considered at the final hearing.”NADA argued that it does not want to send a dope-tainted athlete to the Games. The sample collected on May 10, during the Indian Athletics Series 2 in Chennai, returned an Atypical Finding (ATF) for clomifene. The estimated concentration was reported as 0.032 ng/mL, which is below the Minimum Reporting Level (MRL) of 2.0 ng/mL specified by World AntiDoping Agency (WADA). NDTL suggested an investigation to explain the ATF. Following an investigation, NADA issued a decision on Aug 14, classifying the ATF as an Adverse Analytical Finding (AAF). A notice proposing a two-year period of ineligibility was issued on Sept 2. “I’m hopeful of competing at the Asiad,” Pal, who was represented by Parth Goswami and Niharika Tiwari, told TOI.Meanwhile, AFI sources said, “Based on the NADA panel’s interim directions, AFI will again discuss Pal’s case. No one else (other than Gulveer Singh) has qualified in the men’s 5,000m and 10,000m,” they added. Pal clocked 13:33.95s in Belgium in May to meet the AFI’s qualification mark of 13:39.18s in the men’s 5000m.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Asian Games: Hurdler Nandhini came close to quitting, but never gave up
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: CHENNAI: There was a time when 100m hurdler K Nandini and national-record holder Jyothi Yarraji would often trade places on the podium in age-group ca.
articles.body: CHENNAI: There was a time when 100m hurdler K Nandini and national-record holder Jyothi Yarraji would often trade places on the podium in age-group categories. While Jyothi found the right guidance and surged ahead, Tamil Nadu’s Nandhini struggled, eventually forcing her to quit athletics for nearly four months in 2023.Three years later, the 27-year-old is headed to the Asian Games after rebuilding her career. She clocked a personal best of 13.22 seconds at the Inter-State meet in June to breach the Asiad qualifying mark and followed it up by finishing on top at the recent Indian Athletics Series Final.“I have been waiting for this opportunity for a long time. Like I approach other competitions, I will approach the Asian Games in the same way and not put myself under pressure. The aim is to clock below 13 seconds, and I am able to do that in training,” Nandhini told TOI.She had to train on her own for three years after her coach, Nagarajan, with whom she had trained for nearly a decade, left due to personal reasons. She was in search of a coach but could not find one who could take her to the next stage before joining hands with Pradeep from Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT).“Training alone, it was hard to motivate myself. It was during this period that I quit sports and started preparing for the Income Tax exam. I took the decision because I felt like I was wasting time and that age was catching up. In between, I received a call letter for Income Tax recruitment through the sports quota, and they asked me to come for trials. I did not want to let this opportunity go, so I slowly started training again. But I could not make it.“I deliberately did not attend many competitions because I knew I would not perform well. Coach Pradeep had good knowledge and was working elsewhere. I was waiting to train under him, but his appointment at the SDAT was delayed. Once we got together, we did not try to improve my timings quickly because my technique was poor and I was mentally very weak. He understood what I needed. I did not win any medal for eight months but believed in the process. While I could not medal, I kept improving my timings slowly.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Gukesh on Board 4: Top-board gold medallist in last two Olympiads faces new challenge
articles.summary: Chess News: Defending champions and top seeds Team India have sprang a big surprise even though it’s backed by current form and rating logic. Whether that was nee.
articles.body: Defending champions and top seeds Team India have sprang a big surprise even though it’s backed by current form and rating logic. Whether that was needed or would necessarily hamper the planning of their chief Olympiad rivals is the big question.D Gukesh, who had amassed 18 points in 21 games and two individual gold medals on the top board in the last two editions, has been assigned to play on the fourth board in the biennial team event at Samarkand, Uzbekistan, that began on Wednesday. R Praggnanandhaa (2761), Arjun Erigaisi (2759) and Nihal Sarin (2718) will play on the top three boards.Some surprise element was expected in India’s board order as captain N Srinath did not reveal his cards till 11pm on Tuesday night.To get designated on the fourth board is an unprecedented situation for the reigning world champion (Gukesh) in the history of Olympiad. But then Gukesh has an intense relationship with the unprecedented - becoming the classical matchplay world champion at age 18 and then slipping to Elo 2702 and outside world’s top-30 two years later. That included some wooden spoons in elite events too.Thankfully, Gukesh and the inform Praggnanandhaa, who skipped the exhibition-like GCL in Bengaluru that ended on Sunday, have got more rest than the majority of other elite players. Pragg on the top board is an interesting prospect too.It is unclear if India arrived at the board order as a strategy - to play Arjun in the top half and Gukesh in the bottom half (very different from the last Olympiad) - or, if the players and captain Srinath failed to reach a consensus and followed the Elo rating sequence. “No comments on the board order now,” Srinath told TOI. “Team is motivated and upbeat. Delay in getting rooms was quite unfair and upsetting. But it’s behind us and we will focus on chess now.”Two years ago, Srinath was more than ready to explain his decision to demote Arjun to the third board and promote Pragg to the second. Seven-time Olympian Praveen Thipsay said, “If I was playing a strong tournament or a strong match that Gukesh is playing (World Championship against Sindarov in Geneva from Nov 24), I would prefer my preceding tournament (to be) against stronger opponents so that I am ready for the big challenge ahead.“But my personality may not be like that of Gukesh. In the present scenario (playing on board 4), even if Gukesh scores successive wins in the initial five-six rounds, more than the wins, the manner of his wins and quality of play will determine if he regains the valuable confidence or not."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco destaca el espectacular rendimiento de Karim Adeyemi y apunta a Deco
articles.body: El Barcelona continúa lanzado y su actuación ante el Racing de Santander provocó los elogios de David Sánchez en La Tribu. El presentador de Despierta San Francisco no sólo situó al conjunto de Hansi Flick como una de las grandes referencias del momento, sino que puso el foco especialmente en un nombre: Karim Adeyemi. "No hay ninguna duda. Nadie la tenía, pero después del partidazo ayer del equipo de Flick ante el Racing de Santander, supongo que ya nadie duda de que el mejor equipo de España y seguramente de Europa hoy es el Barcelona", arrancó David Sánchez. Una afirmación que justificó por el rendimiento global del conjunto azulgrana: "Por cómo juega, por lo que genera, por cómo rinden los titulares y por cómo rinden los suplentes". Para David, "todo le sale a pedir de boca al equipo de Hansi Flick", que además "va camino de récord". Entre todos los nombres propios del Barcelona, David Sánchez quiso detenerse especialmente en Karim Adeyemi. "A los nombres de Lamine, de Raphinha y de Rodri, hemos de apuntar ya el de Karim Adeyemi", señaló. Y su valoración del alemán fue contundente: "¡Qué fichaje! Espectacular el rendimiento del alemán". David considera además que Adeyemi "está haciéndose con un puesto en el equipo titular del Barcelona". El precio de la operación también fue destacado por el colaborador de La Tribu. "Descomunal el rendimiento del alemán, que costó solo 22 millones de euros, una medallita para Deco", aseguró. David Sánchez fue incluso más allá al hablar de lo que puede aportar Adeyemi al equipo de Flick. El alemán, a su juicio, "puede ser esa pieza o una de las piezas que le faltaba al equipo para asaltar la Liga de Campeones". Todo dentro de un Barcelona cuyo rendimiento está sorprendiendo a David. El colaborador recordó sus números goleadores: "33 goles en 7 partidos de Liga. Una auténtica barbaridad", antes de mencionar el récord del "Madrid de Mourinho, Cristiano y compañía". David cerró su intervención con otra contundente declaración sobre el momento del Barça: "No hay ninguna duda, seas barcelonista o no, que el equipo que más divierte, el equipo que mejor juega y el equipo que está maravillando al mundo viste de azulgrana, lo entrena Flick y se llama Barcelona".

articles.title: How China’s Asian Games cricket campaign ended without a ball being bowled as Bangladesh advanced to the semis
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: China’s women’s cricket campaign at the Asian Games ended in agonising fashion on Thursday, without the team even taking the field, as their quarter-f.
articles.body: China’s women’s cricket campaign at the Asian Games ended in agonising fashion on Thursday, without the team even taking the field, as their quarter-final against Bangladesh was abandoned without a ball being bowled because of a wet outfield in Nisshin, Aichi prefecture.The T20 match at Korogi Sports Park was called off without the toss taking place after persistent rain and poor weather conditions made play impossible. With no result possible, Bangladesh advanced to the semi-finals on the basis of their higher international ranking, bringing China’s third Asian Games cricket appearance since 2010 to an abrupt end.Bangladesh are ranked 10th in the ICC Women’s T20I rankings, while China are 36th. Under the Asian Games cricket Playing Conditions, the higher-ranked side advances if a quarter-final is abandoned without a result. The same provision was used at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou, where three of the four women’s quarter-finals involving India, Pakistan and Bangladesh were washed out.Rain ends China’s campaign before it beginsFor China, the outcome was particularly frustrating after making it through to the knockout stage of the eight-team women’s competition. The side had hoped to make an impact on the continental stage but instead saw its campaign end without facing a single delivery in the quarter-final.Heavy weather had affected the Korogi Sports Park area throughout the week, and conditions deteriorated enough on Thursday to force a complete cancellation of play. The venue on the outskirts of Nagoya is hosting all the cricket matches at the Asian Games.Bangladesh, meanwhile, moved into the last four without having to bat or bowl. Nigar Sultana’s side will now face the winner of Friday’s quarter-final between defending champions India and hosts Japan in the semi-finals on September 20.India, led by Harmanpreet Kaur, will begin their title defence against Japan in Nisshin on Friday. The other quarter-final on Thursday pits Pakistan against Thailand at the same venue.Bangladesh eye another medal challengeWith only eight teams featuring in the women’s cricket competition, Bangladesh are now just one victory away from reaching the gold-medal match. Both semi-finals are scheduled for September 20, with the gold-medal match to be played on September 22.Bangladesh’s progression also highlights the importance of the tournament regulations in a weather-hit competition. Rather than using a reserve day for the quarter-final, the Playing Conditions provide for the higher-ranked side to progress when a match is completely washed out.China’s exit means the country’s Asian Games cricket campaign is now over. The Chinese men’s side was not included in the eight-team field, leaving the women’s team as the country’s sole representative in cricket at Aichi-Nagoya 2026.The Games have started several sporting competitions before the official opening ceremony, and cricket is among the events beginning ahead of Saturday’s ceremony.The Asian Games cricket competition will conclude with the women’s final on September 22. On the same day, India’s men’s team, led by Shreyas Iyer, are scheduled to play Japan in a T20I at the Sano International Cricket Ground, around 100km from Tokyo. articles.title: 'We're nowhere near favourites': France's Maxime Vachier-Lagrave says India not the only Chess Olympiad contender
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: The 46th edition of the Chess Olympiad kicked off in style for the French men's team on Wednesday as they secured a clean 4-0 sweep over lo.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The 46th edition of the Chess Olympiad kicked off in style for the French men's team on Wednesday as they secured a clean 4-0 sweep over lower-ranked Tunisia. Maxime Vachier-Lagrave, popularly known as MVL, was absent from action as the Board 1 player was rested, perhaps much needed after a gruelling week of matches in India's Global Chess League (GCL).This time, France's team enters the fray with a solid side featuring MVL, Étienne Bacrot, Maxime Lagarde, Jules Moussard and youngester Marc'Andria Maurizzi. Sébastien Mazé serves as captain.But ask MVL whether France can win the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, and he does not reach for a diplomatic hedge, a motivational cliché or the line about how anything can happen in a Swiss system."We're nowhere near favourites," he told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction. "But we have a good solid team, and I think everyone's really motivated. So that's all I can say, and we're hoping for the best."Then, who are the favourites in his opinion?"There are three main favourites, I think. Even four, I would say. USA, India, China and Uzbekistan," the French grandmaster added.Four teams named without hesitation, France not among them, by the man who will be leading France from its top board. This is not pessimism. Spend twenty minutes with MVL, and it becomes clear that it is something closer to the opposite.He possesses a settled, unsentimental clarity about what he can control and what he cannot, precisely the mindset that has kept him at the sport's summit for the better part of two decades.Chess began as a hobby for MVL"I learned the rules at five years old, and gradually I enjoyed the game more and more and started winning," MVL recalled. "This is always, as a kid, the way you kind of pick up a hobby or passion. The more you win, the more you want to play."What he did not anticipate was permanence."I didn't know at the time that I would still be doing basically only that as my profession thirty years later," he continued. "But here we are, and hopefully I've got a few good years remaining."Even when discussing his own longevity, the 35-year-old declines to overclaim. He is careful, too, not to romanticise the profession, even as he defends the choice that led him into what he now calls "a great decision"."Overall I have it easier, because of course it's something I profoundly love since my childhood," he told this website. "But of course, as every profession, it has some moments of doubt, some moments that are not so easy. I think I made a great decision twenty years back."The MVL philosophyAlong the way, there have been setbacks, but he has learnt to put them aside."For everyone, every sportsman, every chess player, there are moments of doubt, moments where things don't go so well. It's just important not to focus on those moments. But to learn the lessons that need to be learned, and to focus on the moments of enjoyment," he said."An improvement curve cannot be a straight line. It has some ups and downs. You just need to always be looking forwards for the ups."Every time I come to India, in the morning I feel very tired, no matter how I slept.Over the past fortnight, MVL had a good time in India, playing for Mumba Masters, who finished fourth in Season 4 of the GCL, although there has not been much sightseeing for him, why?"Every time I come to India, in the morning I feel very tired, no matter how I slept," he admitted, a little apologetically.Besides chess, little sightseeing and tired mornings in India, he found friends who would wake up late to play board games with him, as well as physical sports such as padel during his free time. Alex Pereira is not a fan of Ciryl Gane .

The Brazilian will tell anybody willing to listen how Gane only defeated him because of illegal shots to the back of the head (watch the finish here) . He's campaigned for a rematch and to have referee Herb Dean sacked. Despite Gane having won the first round, Pereira claims that Gane was "dead tired" and forced to rely on illegal shots to steal the victory.

Unsurprisingly, Pereira is not impressed with Gane's new undisputed Heavyweight title. The French striker was promoted from interim to undisputed champion following Tom Aspinall's vacation of the crown , which only happened after further complications to an eye injury that initially stemmed from Gane's jagged fingernails .

In a post on Instagram, Pereira reacted to the divisional change and had a laugh in the process. Check out his post below:

In the graphic above, Gane's Heavyweight resume is broken down and criticized. It reads, "Lost to Francis [Ngannou], lost to [Jon] Jones, [Alexander] Volkov was daylight robbery, 10 illegal head shots to Potan [sic]." There's also a caption that reads "Same circus, different belt."

In other words, the push for the rematch begins in earnest.

At the moment, signs are pointing to a Gane vs. Pereira rematch as the next Heavyweight title fight. There are other options, however. Notably, Josh Hokit has been raising hell at the idea of being skipped over for a man who has yet to win a UFC fight at Heavyweight. Meanwhile, Alexander Volkov really should have scored the nod over Gane in their rematch. Despite promises that UFC would make it up to him , Volkov still has not fought for the title.

Unfortunately for Hokit and "Drago," money talks, and "Poatan" remains one of the sport's biggest stars.

articles.body:
Florida State (1-1) is coming off a bye week after a 27-24 loss to No. 19 SMU on Labor Day.

Next up for the Seminoles ? A road trip to Tuscaloosa for a rematch with the No. 10 Alabama Crimson Tide , who enter the matchup 2-0.

Kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. on September 19, with the game to be broadcast on ABC.

The last time the Seminoles and Crimson Tide faced off was the 2025 season opener in Tallahassee, a 31-17 upset in FSU's favor.

Florida State is currently a 19.5-point underdog in the matchup, according to FanDuel, with the over/under set at 48.5.

Florida State Seminoles vs. Alabama : How to watch

Florida State will play at No. 10 Alabama (2-0) on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC.

The Seminoles opened the 2025 season with a 31-17 win over No. 8 Alabama, snapping the Crimson Tide's 23-season streak of winning the season opener. FSU allowed just 87 rushing yards, had 3.0 sacks and 7.0 tackles for loss.

Head coach Mike Norvell has five regular-season non-conference victories over SEC teams as Florida State's head coach, the most by any coach over the SEC since 2020. His six wins against the SEC since becoming a head coach in 2016 rank as the 2nd-highest non-conference win total over SEC teams in that span.

Norvell is the only active coach with multiple non-conference regular season wins over SEC programs, beating No. 5 LSU in 2023 and No. 8 Alabama last year.

Florida State ranks 9th nationally and leads the ACC with five takeaways, including a season-high four against No. 19 SMU. The four takeaways and +3 turnover margin were both FSU's highest since a 2022 win over Miami.

Quindarrius Jones forced and recovered a fumble against the Mustangs, one week after his first career interception against New Mexico State. Jones is one of two players nationally with an interception, forced fumble and fumble recovery in 2026.

Both of Jones' takeaways occurred on the opponents' first drive of the game.

Running back Samuel Singleton Jr. is one of five players in the country and one of two in the ACC with a rushing touchdown and multiple receiving touchdowns. He has caught both of FSU's passing touchdowns in 2026, the first receiving scores of his career.

Singleton was the ACC Receiver of the Week after tallying 164 all-purpose yards and two touchdowns against New Mexico State. He is the first non-receiver to win the award for Florida State.

Running back Ousmane Kromah and quarterback Ashton Daniels each have rushing touchdowns in consecutive games to begin the season. Kromah is averaging 115.5 rushing yards per game, 2nd in the ACC. He has back-to-back 100-yard rushing games, the first Seminole with consecutive 100-yard games since Trey Benson in 2022.

Kicker Gabe Panikowski is 3-for-3 on field goal attempts this season and is now 18-for-18 on field goals at the NCAA level. He was the Fred Haskins Award winner as the best non-FBS kicker in 2024 when he made all 15 field goal attempts at Idaho State. FSU has made 169 consecutive point after tries, including perfect marks each of the past four seasons.

Florida State is 8-for-8 in the red zone.

articles.title: Anthony Elanga Set To Miss 6-8 Weeks With Hamstring Muscles Injury
articles.summary: The Magpies face a tactical reshuffle as the explosive winger’s Elland Road exit leaves Matthias Jaissle searching for solutions during a crucial stretch of...
articles.body:
Newcastle United are set to be without Anthony Elanga for a significant period after the winger suffered a hamstring injury, with the Sweden international expected to miss around six to eight weeks.

Elanga picked up the injury during Newcastle's recent Premier League defeat to Leeds United at Elland Road, adding to an already difficult evening for Matthias Jaissle's side. The winger was unable to continue and was subsequently withdrawn, with the initial assessment suggesting that the problem could keep him sidelined for a considerable spell.

The injury is a major setback for both Elanga and Newcastle, particularly given the important role the summer signing has been expected to play under Jaissle. His pace, direct running and ability to attack space have been key components of the manager's preferred style, which places a strong emphasis on aggressive pressing, vertical football and quick transitions.

Elanga had made an encouraging start to life at Newcastle and had already demonstrated his ability to provide an additional attacking dimension from wide areas. His ability to stretch opposition defences and carry the ball at speed gives Newcastle an option that is difficult to replicate elsewhere in the squad.

A six-to-eight-week absence would potentially rule Elanga out of a significant number of Newcastle fixtures. Depending on his recovery, the winger could miss a large portion of the early autumn schedule before potentially returning after the next international period.

Newcastle will now have to manage the situation carefully. Hamstring injuries can vary considerably in severity, and the club will be keen to avoid rushing Elanga back before he has fully recovered. The rehabilitation process will therefore be closely monitored by Newcastle's medical staff before a return to full training is considered.

The timing is particularly unfortunate for Jaissle, who is still attempting to establish his preferred system and find the right balance within his Newcastle squad. Elanga's absence removes one of the manager's most naturally explosive options and could force changes to his attacking setup.

It could also create opportunities for other players to step forward. Bazoumana Touré has impressed during his cameo appearances so far and has been pushing for increased involvement. With Elanga unavailable, the Ivorian winger could find himself competing for more minutes, while Harvey Barnes and other attacking options may also be asked to shoulder additional responsibility.

Newcastle's upcoming schedule means squad depth will be tested, with Jaissle likely to rotate his attacking players while attempting to maintain the intensity he demands from his team.

For Elanga, the immediate priority will be making a full recovery rather than focusing on a specific return date. If the projected six-to-eight-week timeframe proves accurate, Newcastle supporters could potentially see him return towards the latter part of the autumn.

Until then, Jaissle must find a solution to compensate for the loss of one of Newcastle's most dangerous pace outlets.

The injury represents another early test for Newcastle's new head coach and his squad. With Elanga facing a prolonged spell on the sidelines, the coming weeks could provide an important opportunity for Newcastle's other attacking players to establish themselves and demonstrate that the team can cope without one of its key summer additions.
