articles.title: Mets players are delusional with their whiny complaints about fans cheering Pete Alonso's 300th HR
articles.summary: The New York Mets got swept at home by the Baltimore Orioles in what was an emotional three days for the fans at Citi Field as they welcomed back Pete Alonso...
articles.body:
The New York Mets got swept at home by the Baltimore Orioles in what was an emotional three days for the fans at Citi Field as they welcomed back Pete Alonso , who left the team in free agency this past offseason.

It was evident from the jump just how beloved Alonso is in Mets territory, and it reached a point where Mets fans were cheering him on even though he hit a game-tying home run in the ninth inning of their contest on Tuesday in a game they lost in extra innings, 7-5.

This long ball was the 300th home run of Alonso's career, and considering that he hit the first 264 dingers of his big-league career with the Mets during his seven-season stint with the team, it's understandable as to why fans reacted the way they did. Alonso did cost the Mets the game, but the fanbase's love for him is so strong that they didn't even care.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

This struck a chord with some Mets players, who couldn't believe what they were seeing. Sean Manaea , who started for New York on Tuesday, even said that he has never seen anything like it throughout his time in the big leagues. It can be jarring for some players to see their own fans turn against them.

However, the Mets players have to know the entire context of this situation . Rooting for Alonso, and by extension, the Orioles, doesn't necessarily mean that they are rooting against the home team.

Make no mistake about it, Alonso is going to receive cheers from the Citi Field crowd no matter what. But if the Mets were in the hunt for a postseason spot, the reaction to his game-tying home run may not have been as warm. However, New York is not in the playoff race, and one loss doesn't really matter in the grand scheme of things, at least from the fans' perspective.

The Mets fanbase is simply expressing its disappointment with the front office for letting Alonso walk in the first place. They had a few opportunities to sign Alonso to a big deal. In 2025, they reached a compromise, with the 30-year-old first baseman signing a two-year, $54 million contract with a player option for 2026.

The slugging first baseman ended up having a solid 2025 campaign, putting up 38 home runs and 126 runs batted in as they barely missed the postseason. And then in 2026, Alonso, now in his 30s, opted out and was looking for the first huge long-term contract of his career, and the Mets hesitated .

This paved the way for the Orioles to sign him to a five-year, $155 million contract. All along, New York simply did not give Alonso that kind of financial respect, perhaps out of their worry that he wouldn't age gracefully. In 2023, they reportedly offered him a seven-year extension worth a total of $158 million, which goes to show how much they tried to penny-pinch with him.

Making matters worse for the Mets is that they used their budget this offseason to sign Bo Bichette to a three-year, $126 million contract (AAV of $42 million). Bichette is only 28, and he is playing a position of greater defensive importance (third base).

Even then, Bichette has underperformed in his first season in New York (16 home runs, 74 runs batted in, 1.7 fWAR). Meanwhile, Alonso keeps on producing, as he now has 37 home runs and 102 RBIs this year and he already has his best fWAR total since his rookie campaign (4.1).

Again, the greatest panacea to all of this is to win baseball games. That's what the Mets players should keep in mind so they can ease the heartbreak fans feel whenever they see a beloved former player continue to tear it up for another team.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels responds to Terry McLaurin's lack of targets
articles.summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels on Terry McLaurin's lack of targets.
articles.body:
In the Washington Commanders ' season-opening loss to the Philadelphia Eagles , one stat stood out above all others. Wide receiver Terry McLaurin caught just two passes for 14 yards. His first catch didn't come until the fourth quarter, and he had all four targets.

Remember when David Blough was promoted to offensive coordinator; he promised to give McLaurin 10 targets per game. So, what happened?

It's not as simple as it seems. Quarterback Jayden Daniels was under intense pressure from start to finish. Philadelphia defensive coordinator Vic Fangio was more aggressive than normal, pressuring Daniels on 50% of his 38 dropbacks. Remarkably, Daniels was sacked only once, but even when he bought time to work through his progressions, there was often no one open. This was especially true in the first half.

Philadelphia has arguably one of the NFL's best secondaries, and while Daniels and Blough finally got the offense going in the fourth quarter, the Eagles were determined not to let McLaurin beat them. Fangio often used a safety to bracket McLaurin. Philadelphia cornerbacks Tariq Woolen and Quinyon Mitchell played well, too, but they had some help.

What did Daniels think of McLaurin's lack of targets?

The quarterback understands how important it is to get the ball to McLaurin, but he also won't force the issue because he has other talented weapons.

"I think we just have answers for that, and you try to predict what you could see," Daniels said when asked how the Commanders would handle extra attention on McLaurin.

"You're not gonna get every answer to the test right, but you try to have predictions of, like, this could happen, and obviously Philly did a great job with their game plan of taking Terry away and forcing other guys to make plays, which they did. And when those opportunities present itself for Terry to make plays, we gotta make them at the end of the day. I gotta give him a good ball, he gotta catch it, a lot has to go on to successfully have a play. But moving forward, man, we just have answers for that, and not gonna force-feed Terry the ball, but still go through my reads, but when those opportunities present itself for Terry to go make plays, I know he'll make them."

That's a very mature response from Daniels. That's leadership. And there will be headlines out there that will not give you the entire quote. Daniels wasn't saying it with any slight towards McLaurin. You want your quarterback, especially a young quarterback, to go through his progressions and find the open man. McLaurin is not a diva. He's a team-first guy and understands this better than anyone.

Sometimes, you just have to tip your hat to the other team. The Eagles made it a point not to allow McLaurin to beat them. It worked. Fortunately for the Commanders, they now have Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams on the roster to help McLaurin.

articles.title: 49ers news: Christian McCaffrey gets 100% real about head-turning rookie
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers star running back Christian McCaffrey is accustomed to carrying a massive workload, but Week 1 delivered a surprising twist to start the...
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers star running back Christian McCaffrey is accustomed to carrying a massive workload, but Week 1 delivered a surprising twist to start the season. During San Francisco 's dominant 27-7 victory over the Los Angeles Rams , rookie running back Kaelon Black turned heads by taking on a featured role in his official NFL debut.

While fans expected McCaffrey to hog nearly all the backfield snaps, Black surprisingly led the team in carries. According to the box score, the rookie out-carried McCaffrey 14 to 10, turning those touches into 65 rushing yards alongside one catch for five yards. Meanwhile, McCaffrey remained sharp and efficient, racking up 68 rushing yards on his 10 carries while adding five receptions for 20 yards in the passing game.

Rather than feeling threatened by the unexpected backfield split, McCaffrey offered glowing praise for the young rusher. Speaking after the game, the All-Pro superstar kept it 100% real about Black's work ethic, intelligence, and rapid progression.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Yeah, I mean that's the standard. Bobby T emphasizes being a complete back, being able to run it, catch, block, and he came in and since Day 1 he's been on his P's and Q's, and so good to where you can trust him with doing anything," McCaffrey said, shouting out running backs coach Bobby Turner.

Earning trust in head coach Kyle Shanahan's complex offensive system is no easy task, especially for a rookie entering his first pro game. Yet, Black stepped up immediately, proving he can handle blitz pickups, pass protection, and tough interior yards.

Establishing a reliable secondary option in Black is fantastic news for San Francisco. Lightening McCaffrey's heavy weekly burden helps keep the superstar healthy for a deep postseason run while giving the 49ers a relentless one-two punch. If Black keeps building on this impressive debut, San Francisco's offense will be nearly impossible to slow down.

articles.title: The Outlook - Week 2 (DET-BUF, MIN-CHI, CAR-ATL, PHI-TEN)
articles.summary: The Outlook is The Huddle's new matchups column. Kevin Tompkins will break down every fantasy-relevant player from each team every week.
articles.body:
We are through one week of the NFL season, and it makes sense to want to take everything at face value since it's the only true data point that we have so far about this season. While there ARE things that we can take from last week's games, we have a lot to learn about players, teams, their tendencies and a lot more. We're not going to overreact about every single thing that happened in Week 1, but we can take a measured approach while understanding that priors we held before the season have changed, can change and will likely change.

"The Outlook" will give you details, stats, angles, recommendations and everything else you need to know to help you make your fantasy football decisions. Every fantasy-relevant player on each team playing will be profiled in this article. We want everybody reading this to bring home championships in your fantasy leagues! This week is the first step!

I am incredibly excited to bring this article to all of you this season and hope you all enjoy the ride. If you have any questions, feel free to find me on Bluesky (@ktompkinsii.bsky.social) and tag me in a post to ask me any lineup questions you have, and I will do my best to get them answered for you.

Let's get into it for Thursday night and through the multiple blocks of this article, this Sunday/Monday full slate of games!

(All game/implied point totals listed were compiled via DraftKings Sportsbook on Tuesday afternoon for DET/BUF and Tuesday night for CAR/ATL, MIN/CHI and PHI/TEN)

Detroit Lions at Buffalo Bills — 8:15 PM ET

Implied Point Total: Bills 29, Lions 24.5

Goff was 26-of-39 for 206 yards and two touchdowns, leading an extremely condensed Lions offense to a win over the New Orleans Saints in overtime in Week 1. How condensed? Only three wide receivers and eight offensive players even took a snap. If you had just looked at the box score after the fact, you would never know that it was a 7-0 score at halftime. Even though the Lions ended up scoring 31 points, it was really Jahmyr Gibbs that did most of the damage rather than Goff, who still threw two touchdowns to Amon-Ra St. Brown. Goff was QB17 on the week, but the upcoming Bills defense did just allow 31 points to the Houston Texans, so maybe some upside here on Thursday night?

Fantasy Advice: For Thursday night against the Bills, Goff is definitely in play as a low-end QB1 for Buffalo's first game at the new Highmark Stadium.

Somehow, 186 total yards and two touchdowns wasn't good enough for overall RB1 or RB2 on the week! Nonetheless, a Detroit backfield minus David Montgomery rode Gibbs to the tune of 34 touches. It's pretty clear who the Lions want to be the engine of their offense. Backup Sione Vaki is the handcuff here, as he touched the ball three times.

Fantasy Advice: You don't need me to tell you to start Gibbs. He's in your lineup if he's active.

St. Brown continued his assault on opposing defenses in Week 1, where he logged 14 targets, catching 10 of them for 67 yards. In typical ARSB style, they were at a 5.2-yard aDOT, but who are we to complain? St. Brown is one of the most bankable receivers in fantasy, and no opponent changes that.

Fantasy Advice: I don't think you don't need me to tell you to start St. Brown in Week 2. Lock him in this week against the Bills.

Williams was plenty involved and ran an equal 95% route participation with St. Brown in Week 1. He was their downfield threat, posting a 14.2-yard aDOT, but only caught 4-of-9 targets for 45 yards and JUST missed a touchdown as well early in Week 1, as he was down at the 1-yard line before Gibbs plunged in for the score. No other Detroit pass-catcher had more than a 5.7-yard aDOT (LaPorta), so the downfield role was clearly his, and he didn't have to fight any other ancillary pass-catchers for those particular targets given how concentrated the personnel is for the Lions. The Bills gave up four completions of 20+ yards in their win against the Houston Texans in Week 1, so perhaps that could be the avenue to exploit the Bills in Week 2?

Fantasy Advice: Williams is a solid low-end WR2. He might seem like your classic boom-or-bust profile. HOWEVER, there's much more volume in store for Williams, given how condensed the target tree is in Detroit.

It wasn't a super interesting day for LaPorta on the stat sheet, but as we've been harping on, it's a condensed offense. Considering only 2-of-36 targets went to a player that wasn't St. Brown, Williams, Gibbs or LaPorta, that's something you love to see. Better days are ahead for LaPorta in this offense.

Fantasy Advice: LaPorta is still a firm low-end TE1 given the offense he's in and his placement within it.

Allen was awesome in Week 1 against what we all thought was a brutal matchup in the Houston Texans' defense. Two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and 334 yards passing; Allen could do no wrong. Sporting the best air yards/att. (12.8 yards) of all quarterbacks in Week 1, he's using the entire field. There's no scenario where you're not starting anybody else over Allen in a given week.

Fantasy Advice: To repeat the last sentence from above: There's no scenario where you're not starting anybody else over Allen in a given week.

In Week 1, the Bills were a little less pass-curious than I think anybody, with that point being driven home more emphatically in a game where both the Bills and Texans scored 30+ points apiece. With two touchdowns on the ground by Allen and a lot of the work through the air later in the game, Cook was present and accounted for but didn't factor too much into the outcome in the third and fourth quarters — outside of catching a couple of his passes then. Cook will have his weeks, but it just wasn't in the cards for Buffalo's season opener.

Fantasy Advice: Keep Cook locked in as your fantasy RB1, as touchdown variance should shift into Cook's favor sooner rather than later.

Is it time for me to ALREADY get my face pushed into the dirt for Moore? Moore led the Bills in targets (seven) and put up a 5-100-1 line on 81% route participation. His touchdown catch probably should have been stopped by somebody, with Texans S Reed Blankenship diving to tip it but ultimately missing and letting Moore go untouched for the final 20 yards to the end zone. That said, Moore took a little more than a quarter of Allen's targets, which is a nice baseline for fantasy production. I'm still slightly skeptical, though, if Buffalo will be passing like this going forward. For Moore's fantasy managers, at least for one week, it was a great sign.

Fantasy Advice: Against the Lions in Week 2, Moore is a solid, low-end WR2, where you're hoping his Week 1 establishes a floor of how much Allen is willing to look his way.

Shakir put up a 4-50-0 line on five targets but saw a couple of downfield looks in addition to his typical line-of-scrimmage targets that have become his signature. He had a target inside the 2 that could have been an easy touchdown but was tipped away and then had another red-zone target in the middle of the fourth quarter as well. Despite running just 63% routes in Week 1, Shakir was schemed up and is the CLEAR WR2 here behind Moore, but one that has solid opportunity each week.

Fantasy Advice: More of a flex play against the Lions in Week 2, but Shakir tends to punch up a bit with his fantasy value, especially in PPR formats.

I am VERY interested in Kincaid moving forward if this is how he's going to be utilized. Sure, he was a 69% route participation (which would have been a season-high last season) against the Texans in Week 1, but he made his looks count with a 5-130 line on six targets. Kincaid was 50% in the slot and 29% out wide in his alignments in Week 1, so getting Kincaid in space and letting him navigate is what we've wanted from him for YEARS.

Considering Kincaid ran the second-most routes on the team after Moore, I'm hoping this utilization sticks because this is how you get to be a top fantasy tight end. We know the offense can support a clear second target and the Bills are going to score a LOT. Kincaid is one of my favorite storylines to follow through the season for Week 1. If you like having fun, Kincaid is most definitely FUN.

Fantasy Advice: The Lions allowed 14 targets, seven receptions, 87 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1 to Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant last week. With that in mind, we're locking in Kincaid as a mid-range TE1 and I don't think that is overdoing it.

articles.title: Ex-Colorado athletics employee admitted to misusing Nike funds year before arrest
articles.summary: Ex-Colorado athletics employee admitted to misusing Nike funds at the school several months before his hiring as CFO of USA Swimming
articles.body:
The former University of Colorado athletics department employee who is facing theft and embezzlement charges in Boulder admitted to misusing Nike funds at the school four months before his hiring as the chief financial officer of USA Swimming in December 2025 , according to an internal university audit report obtained by USA TODAY Sports.

The former employee, Cory Randall Hilliard, 54, is facing three criminal counts related to his administration of the university's Nike Elite program, which provides athletic department employees with funds to purchase Nike merchandise.

"I did it. I admit it," Hilliard told the university's audit department on July 30, 2025, according to the internal audit report.

The audit report was dated Aug. 7, 2025. Hilliard left his job at the university the same month, according to his LinkedIn account. He later was hired as the CFO of USA Swimming in December 2025. He then resigned from USA Swimming after his arrest on these charges in August 2026 , one year after the audit report.

Hilliard is accused of overspending his Nike gear allotment by $9,500 from fiscal year 2022 through the fiscal year ending in June 2025. Any admission to the university's audit department is not the same as pleading guilty in court, which he has not done. He is due to be arraigned in Boulder in October, where he is expected to enter a plea then. His attorney declined comment when reached by USA TODAY Sports.

What happened with these Nike funds at Colorado?

The university's internal report noted how each full-time athletics department employee at Colorado is allotted a certain amount of funds to spend on Nike gear in an online account. This employment perk is part of the university's sponsorship contract with Nike and included an allotment of $621 to $625 annually for employees like Hilliard from 2022-25.

Hilliard served as administrator of this Nike program and could adjust his allocation for the Nike Elite account at any time "without anyone else knowing," according to the report. He overspent his allotment every year from 2022 to 2025, including by $6,011 in 2025 and $2,304 in 2024, the report stated. The report said Hilliard's actions resulted in the loss of $9,501.50, "which could have been used for CU sports teams."

"When questioned if he spent over his allotted $625, he said he did, but it was to purchase Christmas gifts, such as bags and luggage, for the staff within the CU Department of Athletics," the report said. "When IA (internal audit staff) informed Hilliard that the orders for Nike items purchased appeared to be mostly for the men's items in the same size, either large or extra-large, and the men's pants with a size 36-32, Hilliard admitted that he had purchased those items for himself. Hilliard said he could not put a percentage on the total number of items he purchased for himself versus the items he purchased for the staff. Hilliard said he did not have permission to exceed his allotted amount of $625."

University audit report states employee was 'remorseful'

The report noted that from Aug. 21, 2024 to June 27, 2025, Hilliard made 59 orders through his Nike Elite account valued at $6,636 wholesale, all of which were sent to his home address except one. That's $6,011 more than his allotted amount of $625 for fiscal 2025.

"When asked why he overspent his allotted amount, Hilliard said he did so because he had access to the excess Nike Elite funds, and it was an error and a misjudgment by him," the report stated. "Hilliard then said, 'I did it. I admit it.' Hilliard appeared to be remorseful for his actions and told IA that he would be willing to be taxed on the funds over his allotted amount."

The internal audit investigation happened after then-Colorado athletic director Rick George notified the audit department about possible misconduct involving Hilliard in July 2025. At the time, Hilliard had worked at the university for nearly two decades and helped run the athletics department budget.

University police conducted its own independent investigation, which led to criminal charges in August 2026 for theft, embezzlement of public property and first-degree official misconduct.

USA Swimming's hiring history and role in this

It's not clear why USA Swimming didn't know about the internal audit dated nearly four months before his hiring was announced by the organization in December 2025. After his arrest in August 2026, a spokeswoman for USA Swimming said Hilliard was immediately placed on leave without access to any company data or financial controls. The spokeswoman said the organization was conducting an investigation. He resigned the next day.

The spokeswoman told USA TODAY Sports Sept. 14 that there was "nothing new" to report on the case.

Hilliard's hiring at USA Swimming came the same year that the organization had a separate hiring issue with its CEO. The organization announced in February 2025 that Delaware athletic director Chrissi Rawak had been hired for that job. But then Rawak withdrew from it less than 10 days later when the organization learned of a complaint against her at the U.S. Center for SafeSport .

USA Swimming is the national governing body for competitive swimming in the U.S. The organization said then the issue with Rawak was not disclosed to the organization during its "rigorous vetting process" of her.

University of Colorado's history with Nike

Colorado has had a contract with Nike since 1995 and discovered the misappropriated funds during a review of its deal with the company, according to the audit report. That deal was worth $4.75 million in product allotment in fiscal 2025, $90,000 of which was allocated for the Nike Elite program.

The school signed a new five-year deal with Nike in September 2025. Colorado's relationship with the company also played a role in getting head football coach Deion Sanders to return to the Nike fold in 2023 after years of estrangement .

Follow reporter Brent Schrotenboer @Schrotenboer . Email: bschrotenb@usatoday.com

ONE Championship has added a high-profile contest to the ONE Fight Night 48 on Prime Video lineup, pitting two hungry fighters against each other in an atomweight Muay Thai battle that could reshape their promotional trajectories.

Hong Kong's Yu Yau Pui will face the United Kingdom's Marie McManamon at the show, which airs live in U.S. primetime from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, October 2.

Yu's path into Muay Thai began at age 18 as a way to stay fit. The Hong Konger eventually took her first official fight at 22 and never looked back.

She made her ONE Championship debut through the ONE Friday Fights circuit in 2023, reeling off five consecutive victories to earn a US$100,000 contract and a spot on the promotion's global roster.

The 33-year-old made an instant impact in her main roster debut, defeating former ISKA Kickboxing World Champion and WBC Muay Thai World Champion Lara Fernandez in 2024. Since that high point, however, the aggressive striker has hit a rough patch, winning just once in her last four outings.

Five months after knocking out Anna "Supergirl" Jaroonsak and retiring the phenom in Muay Thai action, Yu made the switch to kickboxing and fell to former K-1 Champion Kana "Krusher Queen" Morimoto in a competitive three-round battle this past August. Now holding a professional record of 29-5, Yu looks to rediscover the form that once made her one of the division's biggest threats.

Standing across from her will be McManamon, a 36-year-old representative of the Knowlesy Academy in London, where she trains alongside reigning ONE Bantamweight Kickboxing World Champion Jonathan Haggerty and strawweight phenom Freddie Haggerty .

Widely regarded as one of the United Kingdom's leading Muay Thai strikers, McManamon dominated the domestic scene before making her high-profile ONE Championship debut in 2025, challenging Allycia Hellen Rodrigues for the ONE Women's Atomweight Muay Thai World Title.

The Brit came up short via fourth-round TKO in that outing, and months later, she fell to two-time WBC Muay Thai World Champion Selina "Teep Queen" Flores by unanimous decision.

Now, McManamon looks to re-ignite her ONE Championship career against a fellow veteran who is also motivated to earn a statement victory at ONE Fight Night 48 on Prime Video.

articles.title: Why Barenaked Ladies are singing Canadian national anthem in NFL first
articles.summary: The Bills' new stadium will open with a unique performance from the Barenaked Ladies.
articles.body:
Josh Allen is the main attraction as the Bills open their new stadium on Thursday night, but he isn't the only form of entertainment on hand for the Buffalo faithful.

While OneRepublic will be performing at halftime for the crowd, fans will hear a performance of the Canadian national anthem from rock band Barenaked Ladies.

The Canadian band once threw out the first pitch at a Blue Jays game north of the border, but they are headed just south of the border to help ring in $2.1 billion Highmark Stadium as the Bills host the Lions .

Here's what you need to know about the band and their performance.

Why Barenaked Ladies are singing Canadian national anthem

For the first time, the Bills will play "O Canada" before their home game despite the NFL not having any Canadian teams. That's something the NHL's Buffalo Sabres, who are also owned by Terry Pegula, already do regardless of whether a Canadian team is playing.

Buffalo sits just across the Niagara River from Canada, so the franchise has devoted itself to building a Canadian fan base over the years. Those efforts included games in Toronto during the late 2000s and early 2010s.

With tensions palpable between the U.S. and Canada due to trade disputes, the Bills appear to be extending an olive branch to their neighbors to the north (and west) as they open their new stadium.

So, why the Barenaked Ladies? The band is Canadian, after all, hailing from the Toronto suburbs, and they are one of the top Canadian bands to break through in the United States as well, giving some crossover appeal with a predominantly American audience watching at home.

Here's more to know about the Barenaked Ladies.

The Barenaked Ladies are an alternative rockband that was formed by Ed Robertson and Steven Page in 1988. Robertson remains the band's lead singer.

The band gained popularity in Canada in the early-to-mid 1990s and started to develop an American audience in the late 1990s. Barenaked Ladies' 1998 album "Stunt" featured hit single "One Week," which remains the band's most recognizable song.

As for their name, it came about while Robertson and Page attended a Bob Dylan concert in 1988, Page told the Los Angeles Times in 1992.

"We sat there and talked about all these fake bands we'd like to be in, and started coming up with dumb names for them. I don't know which of us said 'Barenaked Ladies,' but we laughed our heads off," Page said . "It's something we'd say when we were 9 or 10 years old, a phrase we'd forgotten, so it was charming when it popped back up."

When it came time to form a band, the name was brought up again and stuck. True to their name, Barenaked Ladies regularly incorporates humor into their songs and performances.

Despite developing an American audience, the Barenaked Ladies remain popular in Canada and were inducted into the Canadian Music Hall of Fame in 2018. The band is still active, having released a new song earlier this year.

The Barenaked Ladies were formed in Scarborough, Ontario, Canada, a northwest suburb of Toronto. Both Robertson and Page are originally from Scarborough, and three of the four current members are from Scarborough; all are Canadian.

The Barenaked Ladies' most popular song remains "One Week," which reached No. 1 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart in 1998. Despite being released 28 years ago, it has been streamed on Spotify over four times more than any other song by the band.

"If I had $1,000,000," released in 1992, is also one of the band's most memorable hits, incorporating humor into the lyrics, while 2000 single "Pinch Me" was nominated for a Grammy Award.

2013 single "Odds Are" stands as one of Barenaked Ladies' most popular modern songs, but they might be best known by some as the singers of the "Big Bang Theory" theme song that plays at the start of episodes.
